craft_notes: Sthāyin: smell-bow (circle complete). Rows: row 2 (honors→bow). Close: bow (ever-I-bow: the circle closes on bowing). Rejected: 'fragrance' singular — killed: scents kept (parimala plural, varied); 'always' moved — killed: ever kept in bow-line (sadā/satatam refrain).

lines: On Īśa's petal throned she Bhairava honors with varied scents,
nose-called Mahālakṣmī, her — ever I bow.
l4.sanskrit_cite: īśadalasthā bhairavamarcayate parimalairvicitrairyā | praṇamāmi sarvadā tāṃ ghrāṇābhikhyāṃ mahālakṣmīm

reads_against.argmap: Who offers smell? → Mahālakṣmī (ghrāṇa/smell, Īśāna petal) offers perfumes; the eight-petalled circle stands complete.
c1_essence: Mahālakṣmī nose-called worshipped with perfumes from the northeast: smelling itself the rite; circle complete.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta settling toward śānta (wonder circling home to rest)
